subject: Latency tolerance rider and order-form language for Atlas Health (MSA/SOW)
messages:
From: Sabrina Vaughn <svaughn@atlashealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency SLA rider request and order-form language

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete request: for our EU production traffic we need a latency tolerance rider attached to the MSA/SOW that specifies a 95th percentile generation latency of <= 150ms for text-generation endpoints at payload sizes up to 1k tokens, measured at the Redwood API gateway in eu-west-1.

Two asks to start the legal/procurement flow:
- Can Redwood provide proposed order-form clause language that we can insert into the SOW? We prefer short, explicit language that maps to your order form fields (model, region, P95 latency, measurement window, credit schedule).
- We also need an operational runbook that explains regional failover behavior and evidence we can request during audit (sample traces, retention window for logs, and escalation contacts).

Timeline: procurement would like a formal proposal + redline-ready doc by next Wednesday (2028-04-26). Please also indicate whether this requires Dedicated capacity, or whether Hosted with the regional fallback policies is sufficient.

Thanks — copying procurement for visibility.

Best,
Sabrina Vaughn
Head of Platform Integrations | Atlas Health
S: +44 20 5555 0109

Attachments: none (procurement requested example clause in your reply)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Sabrina Vaughn <svaughn@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency SLA rider request and order-form language

Hi Sabrina — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (legal/procurement lead) and Karthik (solutions/serving runtime) so we can put together order-form language + an ops package.

Quick answers up front:
- We can draft a one-page rider that maps exactly to the order form and the SOW. I’ll attach an initial working draft for your procurement team to review.
- Operationally, the 150ms P95 target in eu-west-1 is achievable with our optimized serving profiles for the Redwood-XL and Redwood-XL-quant models for payloads <=1k tokens, subject to session-level batching assumptions. We’ll call out recommended burst-protection (10% headroom) and a canary rollout to validate under your traffic.
- Dedicated capacity would give you guaranteed throughput and simpler credit calculations. Hosted can meet the target but we’d need to include a fallback clause (regional failover to eu-central with documented performance delta) and a transient credit schedule during degraded mode.

I’ve attached: proposed-latency-rider_v1.docx (working draft) and a short runbook extract. Internal next steps: Kimberly and Karthik will validate language and evidence items; I’ll coordinate a short call with your procurement to walk through redlines.

Proposed meeting times: Mon 4/22 10:00-11:00 UTC or Tue 4/23 14:00-15:00 UTC — let me know what works for you and procurement.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: proposed-latency-rider_v1.docx (working draft), regional-failover-runbook.pdf (extract)

From: Sabrina Vaughn <svaughn@atlashealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency SLA rider request and order-form language

Thanks Logan — received the draft and runbook extract. A few procurement-level notes / quick redlines from our side:

1) Measurement boundary: procurement will want the metric measured at the ingress gateway in eu-west-1 (client-facing edge) using a 30-day rolling window. Please add explicit sampling/aggregation language so we can replicate figures in audits.

2) Burst tolerance: Atlas prefers a clause that allows for short-term throughput spikes (up to 30% over baseline for 10 minutes) without triggering credit payments, provided Redwood publishes the incident and the mitigation timeline within 2 hours.

3) Evidence & retention: we require 90 days of perf traces and 365 days of operational events (incident summaries, change logs). If those retention levels require additional storage fees, flag them now.

4) DocuSign and procurement timeline: we target signature by Fri 4/26; procurement can accept a DocuSign packet if the redlines are resolved by EOD Thu 4/25.

I’m attaching our annotated redline (atlas-redlines-latency-rider.docx) with inline comments.

Can you confirm whether supporting the 90/365 retention is standard, or if we need to add a compliance add-on? Also please confirm the credit schedule for a Hosted fallback vs Dedicated.

Best,
Sabrina

Attachments: atlas-redlines-latency-rider.docx (annotations)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Sabrina Vaughn <svaughn@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 Apr 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency SLA rider request and order-form language

Sabrina / procurement team — closing the loop with commitments and next steps.

Summary of what we can commit to and what we’ll include in the final rider/order-form packet:
- Measurement: P95 measured at eu-west-1 ingress over a 30-day rolling window; Redwood will publish the aggregation method and provide sample query(s) for your auditors.
- Burst tolerance: we’ll add a "burst allowance" clause (30% over baseline for up to 10 minutes) with an observability trigger requirement (incident post within 2 hours).
- Evidence & retention: we can provide 90 days of perf traces and 365 days of incident metadata as a standard offering for enterprise customers; long-term raw storage for trace payloads beyond 90 days will be a paid add-on — we’ll call this out in the packet.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: Hosted fallback will include a structured credit schedule (sliding credit scale for degraded-mode across region fallback) and requires a mutually agreed runbook for canary activation. Dedicated capacity removes the fallback credit step and simplifies outage credits; we’ll include both templates in the order form and label them clearly.

Action items:
- Kimberly will incorporate Atlas redlines into the order-form language and confirm the credit table by EOD Thu 4/25.
- Karthik will produce a short ops appendix (sample trace queries, measurement code snippets, and the regional failover sequence) by Thu 4/25.
- I’ll prepare a DocuSign packet (link below) once redlines are resolved and coordinate a 30-minute sign-off call.

DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/sign/abc123-latency-rider-proposal
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234560/DEAL-ATLAS-4382

Sabrina — can you confirm procurement availability for Thu 4/25 16:00-16:30 UTC for the final redline walk? If that works we’ll lock it and circulate the DocuSign packet after the call.

Thanks everyone — feel free to reply with final edits.

— Logan
